conviction_note: Each finding is small and they net to 0.0. A stretched consensus (Q3 adj. EBIT 44 MEUR at 11.6%, above Inderes' 41) and the raw-material headwind the company itself flagged for Q3 sit against a likely upward narrowing of the 8-10% margin guide and a 14% de-rating into the print. So the move should be large (9%, on four straight report-day moves of +11.3/+4.9/+2.3/+17.9 and a guidance line that is likely to change), but the sign is close to a coin flip: p_up 51 gives +0.18.

already_public.what: FY2026 guidance (unchanged at H1): net sales to grow and segments operating profit 8-10% of net sales; H1 segments OP 40.7 MEUR (6.2%), Q2 45.0 MEUR (11.8%)
Report date and time: Q3 interim on 27 Oct 2026 at about 13:00 EET, call at 14:00 EET; no profit warning (tulosvaroitus) in either direction on the Nasdaq Nordic feed since the H1 report

new_in_release.expect: Q3 sales and adjusted EBIT are new. The bar is adj. EBIT 44 MEUR / sales 374 MEUR. My lean is slightly below that bar, because the oil and rubber cost increase reaches costs from Q3 while consensus sits above Inderes' 41.

I expect the 8-10% margin guide to be narrowed or raised toward its upper end, about 55% likely (Inderes' FY estimate is 9.9%). Keeping 8-10% unchanged would read as a disappointment. Sign is uncertain, size large.
Comments on the start of the winter season, Hakkapeliitta 01 sell-through and Heavy Tyres forestry demand. Direction unknown.
Q3 operating cash flow is seasonally weak from winter-tire receivables; gearing was 71.8% at H1. Mild negative risk.

findings.finding: The Q3 bar is demanding: consensus adj. EBIT is 44 MEUR at 11.6% (10 analysts, range 41-47), above Inderes' 41 MEUR / 10.9%, while the oil and rubber cost increase that began in spring starts to show in costs from Q3, per the company's own earlier comments as reported by Inderes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarterly beats have been bought, not sold. Q2'26 adj. EBIT 45 vs consensus 32-35: +17.9% on the day (2026-07-17). Q3'25 beat: +11.3% (2025-10-28). Q1'26: +2.3% then +9.6%. FY25: +4.9%.
findings.original_quote: Huomioimme kuitenkin, että keväällä alkanut raaka-ainehintojen (kuten öljyn ja kumin) nousu alkaa yhtiön aiempien kommenttien mukaisesti näkyä kustannuksissa Q3:sta alkaen, mikä rajaa jossain määrin kannattavuuden nousuvaraa. [We note, however, that the rise in raw-material prices (such as oil and rubber) that began in spring will, according to the company's earlier comments, start to show in costs from Q3 onward, which limits the room for margin improvement to some extent.]
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has stayed above the one explicit public forecast that writes in the cost headwind; if the market had reconciled the two, consensus would sit near 41. Part of it may already be in the 14% de-rating over 20 sessions, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: Michelin's 9M release (2026-10-20) says Q3 price increases were a reaction to 'increasing input costs', so the input-cost inflation is industry-wide. https://www.michelin.com/en/publications/group/financial-information-at-september-30-2026

findings.finding: A guidance change is likely: Inderes puts the FY26 adj. EBIT margin at 9.9%, the top of the 8-10% guide, and says the company 'may raise and/or narrow' it with Q3. OP flagged a possible positive profit warning in July, but none was filed before the print, so a raise far above 10% is less likely than an upward narrowing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY26 guide introduced in Feb 2026 brought +4.9% and +4.85% on consecutive days (2026-02-10/11). The guide was reiterated at Q1 and Q2 and the stock still rose on the beats.
findings.original_quote: Koko vuoden marginaaliennusteemme on nykyisen ohjeistuksen (oik. EBIT-% 8-10) ylälaidassa, joten yhtiö voi nostaa tai tarkentaa sitä ylöspäin. [Our full-year margin forecast is at the top of the current guidance (adj. EBIT % 8-10), so the company may raise or narrow it upward.]
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus already sits near 10%, so a mere narrowing to 9-10% is roughly expected, and keeping 8-10% would disappoint. The positive skew only exists because Q4 has been treated as risky (winter season, raw materials) and the stock de-rated 14% into the print. Sign uncertainty keeps this small.
findings.independence: OP note, as quoted on the Inderes forum on 2026-07-20: 'OP uskoo että loppuvuodesta saattaa tulla vielä posari' [OP believes a positive profit warning may still come later in the year]. https://forum.inderes.com/t/nokian-renkaat-oyj/663/3808

findings.finding: Heavy Tyres read-through: Ponsse, a main forestry-machine OE customer, reported Q3 net sales down 7.4% with 'very weak' operational profitability (20 Oct), and Inderes notes Deere's Finnish change negotiations. Heavy Tyres is 20-25% of Nokian's near-term operating profit at a 15% margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated before. Nokian was −0.15% on the Ponsse day (2026-10-20), after −4.57% the previous session.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty read-through, a transmission hypothesis until Nokian comments. Ponsse's order intake rose 19% in Q3, which cuts the other way, and replacement tyres for forestry follow machine hours, not new-machine sales. The net effect is small.
findings.independence: Inderes analyst Rauli Juva on the forum (2026-10-20): 'Metsäkonemarkkinan hiipuminen voi pistää tähän vastatuulta' [the fading forestry-machine market may put a headwind here]. https://forum.inderes.com/t/nokian-renkaat-oyj/663/3835

findings.finding: Michelin's 9M 2026 release (20 Oct): Michelin-brand replacement volumes +4% YTD, price effect turned positive in Q3 as prices rose in reaction to input costs, FY guidance confirmed. Replacement demand and price discipline are holding industry-wide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Michelin fell 7.2% on 2026-10-21; Nokian moved +0.74% that day and did not follow.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for four sessions and Nokian did not react, so it is mostly priced. It mainly corroborates that prices can be passed through.

findings.finding: Tyres Europe Q2 2026 (published Aug): European replacement winter-tyre sell-in fell 1% in Q2 and 5% YTD, while all-season rose 15%. Nokian's own winter share of PCT sales fell to 49% from 55% in H1.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a broad proxy for Q2, not Q3, and Nokian outgrew the market in every region in H1, so it carries little weight.
findings.independence: Nokian H1 report: winter tyres 49% (55%) of PCT sales value. https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b4b0fb04993922c25b2ecbdf60a8700c7&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: The new flagship stud tyre Hakkapeliitta 01 went on consumer sale on 15 Sep 2026 at premium prices, so Q3 is its first sell-in quarter. The CEO said pre-sales were going well (Kauppalehti, 30 Jul). Test results are mixed: a Bilägare test win, 4th among studded tyres in Teknikens Värld.
findings.original_quote: Ajo-olosuhteisiin mukautuva uusi Nokian Tyres Hakkapeliitta® 01 -nastarengas nyt kuluttajien saatavilla [The new Hakkapeliitta 01 stud tyre that adapts to driving conditions is now available to consumers]; forum citing Kauppalehti 30.7.2026: 'ennakkomyynti käy hyvin' [pre-sales are going well]
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-through numbers have never been disclosed. Management's first number or comment on the launch comes in this release, and the mixed magazine tests (Teknikens Värld 4th of the studded tyres) have dampened enthusiasm.
findings.independence: Dagens PS summary of the Nordic tests: https://www.dagensps.se/motor/bast-vinterdack-2026-stor-genomgang-av-nordiska-tester/ ; forum post 2026-07-30: https://forum.inderes.com/t/nokian-renkaat-oyj/663/3819

findings.finding: The EU's definitive anti-dumping duties on Chinese passenger-car and light-truck tyres (Implementing Regulation 2026/1540: 4.3% Hankook, 24.4% other cooperating, 45.3% the rest) have applied since 8 Jul 2026, so Q3 is the first full quarter with them. This supports premium price/mix in Central Europe, where Nokian is regaining share.
findings.why_not_priced: The duties have been public since July. Only their contribution to Q3 pricing is new, and it is likely small within one quarter.

findings.finding: The stock de-rated 14.4% over 20 sessions with no company news: DNB Carnegie cut to hold on 5 Oct (−4.8% that day), with a EUR 16.5 target now 23% above the EUR 13.4 spot, and there was a sector-wide −4.6% on 19 Oct. Disclosed shorts are flat at 3.18% after covering from about 5% in July. The valuation objection behind the downgrades has been partly answered by price, which lowers the bar for the reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (+17.9%) came after a large run-up and a short near 5%. This time the setup has the run-up reversed and the short smaller.
findings.original_quote: DNB Carnegie laskee Nokian Renkaiden suosituksen pidä-tasolle (aik. osta-suositus), toistaa 16,5 euron tavoitehinnan. [DNB Carnegie cuts Nokian Tyres to hold (from buy), reiterates EUR 16.5 target.]
findings.why_not_priced: This partly overlaps the baseline lean (runup +0.72, squeeze +1.91), so it is sized small. What sits outside the lean is that the drawdown came from a broker cut and sector beta, not company news. An unexplained drawdown is worth about 0.

findings.finding: Cash flow is a risk line. Q2 operating cash flow was −2.2 MEUR (16.5 a year earlier) 'mainly due to higher sales driving increased receivables', and net debt was 815 MEUR at 71.8% gearing at H1. Q3 is the seasonal winter-tyre receivable build, and growth makes it bigger.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's negative operating cash flow came with +17.9% on the day, so cash was looked through when profit beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus previews focus on EBIT, and the cash line is rarely in the preview tables. It matters only if profit merely meets the bar.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The baseline lean is +2.6 (squeeze plus run-up reversal), and the de-rating and guidance findings agree with it, but the stretched consensus, the Q3 raw-material headwind and the Heavy Tyres read-through cut against it. The findings net to 0.0 and p_up is 51 rather than leaning with the +2.6.
language_note: The Q3 consensus table (Modular Finance, 10 analysts: adj. EBIT 44, range 41-47) and Inderes' explicit raw-material-from-Q3 caveat came from the Finnish-language Inderes preview; no English source carried the Q3'26 bar
The Ponsse/Deere to Heavy Tyres read-through, the DNB Carnegie downgrade to hold (5 Oct) and OP's 'posari' (positive profit warning) remark came only from the Finnish Inderes forum
The issuer's own releases came in Finnish and English at once and added nothing beyond each other
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide': the guidance finding went from +0.3 to +0.5 and was sized on the guidance scale (about 55% chance of an upward narrowing or raise vs 40% unchanged), and abs_move_pct went from 8 to 9
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': filed the H1 receivables-driven negative operating cash flow and 71.8% gearing as a cash-flow finding (−0.3) that the draft had left out
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': Ponsse read-through went from −0.4 to −0.3 and the Tyres Europe winter proxy from −0.2 to −0.1
'Positioning is the thing to beat': the short is flat at 3.18% and not crowded, so the positioning finding stayed small at +0.3
